mappings.note: Closed flowers force self-pollination (LO-4), and the question asked is what that does to genetic diversity (C-3.3-LO-5). Both cited because the item has a mechanism half and a consequence half; the part-1 selfing item asks only the consequence and takes C-3.3-LO-5 alone.

The purpose of muslin bags in the pea experiment: excluding foreign pollen. Pollination control, LO-4. Not C-5.1-LO-1 despite the draw instruction, because what is drawn is an apparatus, not a reproductive structure.
Artificial hybridisation as a technique. Pollination control end to end; the same outcome as the ordering MCQ, differing only in whether the student recalls the sequence or explains it.

Contrasts wind and insect pollination on pollen output and flower traits, which is exactly the abiotic-and-biotic agent pairing C-4.3-LO-1 names. C-2.8-LO-1 withheld: no interaction consequence is examined, only the adaptations.

POOR FIT. Whether physical maturity implies readiness for parenthood. Third item in the maturity family, all on C5.2; no biology outcome covers adolescent readiness, and LO-10 is about devices, not judgement.

Identifies self and cross pollination from a diagram (LO-4) and then names an agent for the cross-pollination arm (C-4.3-LO-1). C-5.1-LO-1 was dropped to stay within the codes that discriminate: the diagram shows a process, not the structure of a reproductive unit.
POOR FIT. Duration of pregnancy, its division into trimesters, and first-trimester changes. Gestation is entirely uncovered by this frame.

Tissue culture technique and why it matters in agriculture. LO-12 deliberately NOT cited even though it names Indian tissue-culture research: this item names no scientist and no Indian contribution, so citing LO-12 would map the chapter rather than the question.
What STIs are and two ways to prevent them. The prevention half lands on the contraceptive-device limb of LO-10; the definitional half reaches it only through the fused reproductive-health clause.
Why a tomato is botanically a fruit: it is a ripened ovary containing seeds from fertilised ovules. The single cleanest use of the ovary-to-fruit outcome in the chapter.

POOR FIT. Why reproduction is essential for the species though not for the individual. No outcome states the significance of reproduction as such. LO-7 rejected: no asexual/sexual contrast is drawn, unlike the definitional MCQ in part 1 that does draw one.

Reads a flower diagram to identify the male and female parts and their components. C-5.1-LO-1 for working from the illustration, LO-8 for naming the organs and their sub-parts. The matching-table version of the same content takes LO-8 alone.

The discriminating half is how meiosis leads to variation in offspring, which is precisely C-3.3-LO-5. The chromosome-halving half would fall back to C3.3, but the item's second question is what separates it from the pure meiosis items, so the variation outcome is cited alone.
Step-by-step grafting procedure. Method only, so the C3.2 twin; unlike the grafting MCQ about which plant the fruit resembles, nothing genetic is asked, so LO-9 is not engaged.

A hardened egg coat blocks sperm entry, so external fertilisation fails. The mechanism broken is fertilisation itself, so LO-4; the population consequence is downstream reasoning, not the outcome being probed.
POOR FIT. Maternal care and nutrition after childbirth, breastfeeding, newborn warmth. Post-natal care has no outcome anywhere in this frame; LO-10's health clause does not reach it.
Draw an IUD and explain how the Copper-T prevents pregnancy. Contraceptive-device limb of LO-10. C-5.1-LO-1 not added: a device is not a reproductive unit or system.
Three sub-parts, all methods: vegetative propagation, grafting, tissue culture. Uniformly the C3.2 process twin; no sub-part asks about genetic identity, so LO-9 stays out.

Sub-parts (a) and (b) are chromosome halving, which only the competency C3.3 reaches; sub-part (c), long-term survival of the species, is the variation outcome C-3.3-LO-5. Parent and child are both cited because they answer different sub-parts of a five-mark item.

Sub-parts (a) and (b) are the mode of fertilisation (LO-4); sub-part (c), the role of yolk, has no outcome at all, so the competency is added to cover it. Flagged: one third of this item is outside the frame.

Rhizopus diagram, spread by spores, and refrigeration. All three sub-parts are asexual reproduction by spore formation, so LO-7. C-5.1-LO-1 not used: that outcome is about male and female reproductive units, and spore formation has neither.
POOR FIT. What menstruation is and the uterine and ovarian changes across 28 days. The largest single item in the chapter with no learning outcome behind it.

Roles of testes, vas deferens and prostate, then sperm versus egg. Both sub-parts are male and female reproductive organs and their products, so LO-8 alone; no diagram is required, so C-5.1-LO-1 stays out.
The one item that legitimately uses all three: draw and label the flower (C-5.1-LO-1), trace pollination and fertilisation (LO-4), and end at seed formation (LO-3).

STIs, which contraceptives protect against them, and how IUDs and surgical methods work. Every sub-part falls inside the fused LO-10 row, which is why one code covers a five-mark item with four distinct demands.
